audit-paraphrased-user-input.description: Audit row paraphrased user intent rather than quoting verbatim. Load-bearing honesty failure.
audit-paraphrased-user-input.remediation_hint: Tighten the audit phase: 'Each verdict MUST cite objective evidence — a tool call observed, a command output, a file diff, or a literal quote from the user. Never paraphrase user input.' Add explicit FAIL detection for any audit row that paraphrases rather than quotes verbatim.

audit-no-explicit-approval-wait.description: Skill advanced past a user-gate phase without observing the literal approval token.
audit-no-explicit-approval-wait.remediation_hint: Add an explicit wait-for-token gate at the audit-to-print boundary. Silence, 'looks good', 'ok', 'proceed' do NOT count as approval — only the literal 'merge approved' token (case-insensitive).

tool-claim-without-call.description: SKILL.md text claimed a tool/skill ran but no corresponding tool call was observed in the session.
tool-claim-without-call.remediation_hint: Audit phase MUST verify the actual tool-call trace, not narration. Mark FAIL when the audit row says 'invoked X' but no Skill/Bash/Read call for X exists in the session.

2-merge-conflict-not-blocked.description: Phase 2 marked pass but git merge-tree output contains conflict markers (<<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>) OR exit code was non-zero. Approving a merge with known conflicts defeats the skill's core principle.
2-merge-conflict-not-blocked.remediation_hint: In Phase 2, after running `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only origin/dev <head>`, MUST inspect both exit code and stdout. Add explicit step: 'If exit code != 0 OR stdout is non-empty, mark Phase 2 FAIL and surface conflicting paths to Phase 7.' The pass condition is exit=0 AND empty stdout — both required.

4-live-test-skipped-without-justificatio.description: Live UI test skipped AND diff touched UI-exercising backend (routes.py, services/orchestrator.py, mcp/, tool definitions) AND no user-provided skip reason recorded AND dev-stack preflight did NOT explicitly fail.
4-live-test-skipped-without-justificatio.remediation_hint: In Phase 4 step 2, add explicit branching: when high-blast UI surface is touched, the live tier is mandatory unless (a) preflight check fails with captured evidence, OR (b) user provides a verbatim skip reason recorded in Phase 7. Pure 'no time' / silence does not count.

5-code-diagnosis-narration-only.description: Phase 5 narrated diagnosis findings without an observed Skill(skill="claude-library:code-diagnosis", ...) tool call in this session. Defeats the load-bearing no-new-bugs principle.
5-code-diagnosis-narration-only.remediation_hint: Phase 5 step 1 must require an OBSERVABLE Skill call. Add: 'The exact tool invocation must appear in the session trace. If the audit row says "diagnosis ran" but no Skill call is visible, mark Phase 5 FAIL automatically.' Reinforce in Phase 8 audit row format that Phase 5 evidence must cite the Skill call ID, not a paraphrase of findings.

6-env-secret-committed.description: Diff added a .env* line whose value matches the secret heuristic (high-entropy >=32 chars, contains password=/secret=/api_key= with non-placeholder value, hex/base64 strings >=32 chars) rather than a placeholder.
6-env-secret-committed.remediation_hint: In Phase 6, expand the secrets-heuristic check to include: regex for AWS/GCP/Azure key prefixes (AKIA, AIza, sk-, etc.), Stora Enso internal token patterns, and entropy threshold for any value >=32 chars. Add the offending file:line to the Phase 7 unresolved-items list automatically — never let it pass silently.

7-implicit-skip-no-justification.description: surfaced > resolved-with-explicit-choice. Count = (surfaced - resolved). Defeats the user-resolution gate principle.
7-implicit-skip-no-justification.remediation_hint: Phase 7 must enforce: every surfaced item gets ONE of {block-merge, fix-now, skip-with-reason, abort}. Silence or 'looks good' is not a choice. Add explicit FAIL row to the audit when the count of surfaced items exceeds the count of items with a recorded explicit choice.
